name: Samuel Wesley the Younger
bio: Samuel Wesley the younger (1690–1739), the eldest son of the rector of Epworth and elder brother of John and Charles Wesley, was an usher at Westminster School and later headmaster of Blundell's School at Tiverton. He is not to be confused with his father, Samuel Wesley the elder (1662–1735), also a poet.
He wrote hymns, satires and epigrams, collected in Poems on Several Occasions (1736), and was a friend of Francis Atterbury, Bishop of Rochester.

poems.title: From a Hint in the Minor Poets
poems.author: Samuel Wesley the Younger
poems.text:
No; not for Those of Women born,
Not so unlike the Die is cast;
For, after all our Vaunt and Scorn,
How very small the Odds at last!
Him, rais'd to Fortune's utmost Top,
With Him beneath her Feet compare;
And One has Nothing more to hope,
And One has Nothing more to fear.

poems.title: Epigram on Miltonicks: After the Manner of the Moderns
poems.author: Samuel Wesley the Younger
poems.text:
What makes You write at this odd Rate?
Why, Sirs, it is to imitate.

What makes You rant and ramble so?
Why, 'tis to do as others do.

But there's no Meaning to be seen:
Why, that's the very Thing I mean.
